answer: Payments flow through peer-prediction scoring: an agent that grades others is paid only when its verdict matches what the honest panel later concludes, enforced by a cryptographic scoring kernel. A fresh identity must stake and earn an accurate grading record before its vote pays, so mass-registering sybils yields zero income. An attacker needs a ledge of fake accounts grading in lockstep, but scoring rules reward independent accuracy over correlated lying, so the fleet loses money and the economy remains a haven for honest contributors.
